What is the best offline dictionary app for iPhone?

When choosing an offline dictionary for iPhone, check three things: the language of your book, which resources must be downloaded, and whether you want to type a word or scan it with the camera. Test a few lookups in airplane mode after setup.

Booktionary is for looking up words in printed books with the iPhone camera. English definitions are built in. It supports 24 book languages in total, with 23 optional dictionary downloads. One purchase includes the available language packs, with no subscription or in-app purchases.

For books in English, separate word-translation packs add equivalents in 24 target languages. On iOS 18 or later, translated definitions are available for 19 supported destinations after the necessary language files are downloaded. These options do not turn a French or Spanish book dictionary into a full-page translator.

The base app requires iOS 17 or later. Sentence-based meaning selection has an additional requirement: a supported iPhone with Apple Intelligence available on iOS 26 or later. Otherwise, the first dictionary meaning appears and you can explore other meanings. See the current language list and requirements on the Booktionary home page.

Check before reading offline

  1. While connected, select the book language and finish its download.
  2. For an English book, install any optional translation resources you want to use.
  3. Turn on airplane mode and make sure Wi-Fi is off.
  4. Open the app and look up several words from your book. If a resource is missing, reconnect and finish downloading it before leaving.

See the app, all supported languages and download requirements.
